headline: A young Shanghai company, StartLux, has released a free decision-making AI model that it says beats the popular Jev model on most tests.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: the release was on 30 Sep 2026, before 2 Oct, and the scores are the company's own tests with no outside review reported.
importance_line: Developers building AI helpers that act for users get a small free model that can run on their own machines, but the winning scores are StartLux's own runs and have not been checked by outsiders.
summary: 36Kr reports that StartLux, a Shanghai company founded less than five months ago, released its free StartLux-Decision models on 30 Sep 2026; a decision model picks an option such as yes or no instead of writing text, and this continues yesterday's story on Amazon's own copy of the Jev decision model. New today is a Chinese rival: StartLux says its biggest version beat Jev 1.13 on 31 of 38 tests, scoring 63.88 against 57.91, and won 35 of 36 chess games, but these are the company's own test runs.
notes: Continues the 2 Oct 2026 edition's C01-01 (Amazon's Jev clone, TechCrunch 1 Oct 2026). Release date 30 Sep 2026; results are self-reported with a public-ranking snapshot of 28 Sep 2026.
